scope.population: 2480267 taker fills and 45849 wallets; the toxicity ranking is built on wallets with at least 50 fills in the early half and evaluated on the late half, per coin and pooled, and the whole of that once per lens -- the ranking is rebuilt on each reference price rather than carried across, so the screened wallet set is a property of the lens too and not only the cost is
scope.window: days 4-13, split by settings.split_early_late into ranking days [4, 5, 6, 7, 8] and evaluation days [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

override_reasons.master_seed: every random stream here is derived from 20260619, not from the declared 20260620. Derived and not equal: the count-matched null takes 20260619 itself, the size-matched null 20260620, and the joint null 20260621 with the chain index beside it in the entropy, and each block records the number its own generator was built from. This key read 'every random stream here is seeded 20260619' until 2026-08-30, which was true of one stream of three. settings.MASTER_SEED carries the state 'target', so adopting it re-draws all three streams and moves every published placebo number
override_reasons.n_boot: no bootstrap runs in this file; the intervals here are permutation and stratified-draw nulls, so the declared bootstrap budget does not apply
override_reasons.whale_drop_criterion: this file drops the largest wallets by NOTIONAL, answering 'is the reduction a volume artifact'; t3_capacity.py drops by COST, answering 'is it ten wallets'

_meta.object: T1+T2 - counterparty-toxicity-skewed market-making backtest (cost reduction vs a symmetric Avellaneda-Stoikov baseline)
_meta.framing: COST REDUCTION ONLY, NEVER NET ALPHA
_meta.lens_policy: BOTH LENSES ARE PUBLISHED AND NEITHER IS WIRED INTO THE INPUT, since 2026-08-03. Every T1 and T2 block sits under <slice>.by_measure.<lens>, where lens is 'mid' (the book mid, which settings.HEADLINE_LENS declares and which this file leads with) or 'print' (the trade print, which is what this object ran on and published alone until that date). The two are not a rounding apart: the volume-weighted mean 10s markout is 2.2388 bps on the mid against 0.5208 on the print, because the print already contains the spread the maker earned, so a cost measured on it is a cost net of income. The mid is the declared lens because adverse selection is defined in this study against the book mid; the print figure is legitimate on its own terms -- the maker is paid at the print -- and it stays in this file so the earlier versions of this study that quote it go on reproducing. THE KEYS MOVED: what used to be <slice>.t1_early_late_split_10s and .t1_early_late_split_60s and .t2_walk_forward, all three on the PRINT lens without saying so, is now <slice>.by_measure.print.<same name>. Nothing is repeated at the old path on purpose: a path that does not name its lens is the defect this change exists to remove, and leaving one would let a reader take the mid figure from a key that used to hold the print one.
_meta.split_rule: The ranking and evaluation halves are DERIVED from the days present, by settings.split_early_late: first ceil(n/2) days early, the rest late. They used to be the hardcoded day-of-month tuples (4,5,6,7,8) and (9,10,11,12,13), which are correct only for a window opening on the 4th and closing on the 13th. This input does open on the 4th, so the derived split reproduces those tuples exactly and no number moved.
_meta.markout_sign: signed taker markout bps; positive = taker profited = maker adverse-selected; positive cost = maker loss
_meta.oos_split: by TIME - ranking on EARLY days, evaluation on LATE days; no wallet's late data informs its own ranking
_meta.placebo_count_matched: label-permutation of the toxicity ranking, 2000 shuffles, seed 20260619; the null draws a RANDOM set of the SAME NUMBER of wallets. A real reduction must beat a random-ranking maker (placebo p <= 0.05). WEAKNESS: does NOT control for notional - toxic wallets are also large, so this null turns away far less volume and its mean (~6.9%) understates the pure-size baseline.
_meta.placebo_size_matched: draw 1000 random wallet sets matched on TOTAL LATE NOTIONAL of the observed toxic set (10 notional strata, seed 20260620); this null turns away the SAME dollar volume, so its reduction (mean ~30.4% / p95 ~56.6%) is the PURE-SIZE baseline. The Monte Carlo tail probability of the observed toxicity-ranked reduction against THIS null (~0.002) is the share of its draws that reached the observed value under the procedure declared here. It is NOT a demonstration that wallet identity is statistically significant: the draws control HOW-MUCH and the tail says only how rarely they reached the observed cut. A deterministic size-only screen (decline top decile by notional, no toxicity) ~44.9% is also reported.
_meta.placebo_joint_matched: draw 2000 wallet sets holding BOTH axes at once, over 8 independent starts (seed 20260621, the chain index in the entropy beside it): exactly the observed number of wallets, and a total late notional within 1.0 per cent of the observed toxic set's. The two nulls above hold one axis each and let the other run, and passing them separately is not passing one null that holds both, because a set can satisfy either constraint by breaking the other. The sets come from a swap walk that never leaves the region, stepped in ATTEMPTED swaps so the chain is read at fixed times, and mixing single swaps with paired ones because single swaps alone freeze the largest wallet of a set for the whole chain. THE WALK DOES NOT FORGET ITS START ON THIS DATA and nothing here pretends otherwise: the starts disagree about where the null sits on every cell, the spread is published in each block's chain_agreement, and a cell whose starts disagree about the TAIL gets NO number at all. AND THIS NULL PUBLISHES NO P-VALUE ON ANY CELL, which the two above do: a p-value is a probability under a known null distribution, and this one's draws come from a walk whose distribution over the region is not established, as every block of it says in its own claim. What is published instead is joint_matched_tail_fraction_floored, the share of the draws that reached the observed reduction with the observed set counted as one of them, and THREE PLAIN FACTS beside it that carry no threshold: n_draws_at_or_above_observed of n_draws, the largest reduction any draw reached at joint_matched_max_reduction_pct, and the observed value itself at observed_reduction_pct. Until 2026-08-30 the fraction was written under a key ending in _p and beside a flag reading toxicity_beats_joint_matched, which read as the verdict of a test that was never run; no threshold reading replaces it, because a flag saying 'at or below five per cent' would be that same verdict under another name. The counting is unchanged and no number moved with the names. WHY THE STARTS DISAGREE IS MEASURED AND IS PUBLISHED AT region_freedom: the observed set's own largest members carry most of its notional and the pool holds nothing to swap them for one for one, so a draw is largely settled by which large wallets its chain entered with. That is also the caveat this null owes a reader, because the two grow together: the same resemblance that makes it stricter than either single-axis null makes it degenerate where the largest member is large, since every admissible draw is then a near-copy of the observed set. IT SITS HIGHER THAN THE SIZE-MATCHED NULL, NOT LOWER, measured on this run: holding the count as well as the volume forces every draw to resemble the observed toxic set, and a set that resembles it recovers more of its reduction, so this null stands nearer the observed value than either single-axis one. What a surviving cell asserts is that over 8 independent starts holding both axes, no draw reached the observed reduction -- weaker than a uniform null over the region, stronger than either single-axis null. Every block also records the outcome of three calibration cases the region test is run against on that cell's own wallets. It REPLACES NEITHER of the other two.
_meta.fill_model_extension_note: The 'no fill model' objection can be answered by a minimal fill model: recapture a fraction f of declined toxic notional at a widened quote plus a per-requote penalty. NOT implemented here - this object stays a realized-markout counterfactual.
_meta.whale_robustness: drop the 10 largest wallets by notional, re-rank and re-evaluate the headline policy. The block key states both the count and the criterion (whale_robustness_drop_top10_by_notional), because dropping by notional answers 'is the reduction a volume artifact' while dropping by cost answers 'is it ten wallets' -- t3_capacity.py drops by cost and this file drops by notional, and under a key naming only the count the two checks looked interchangeable.
_meta.headline_scope_note: Which slices are defensible headlines is DERIVED from the numbers of this very run and is not declared at this key. Each slice carries a headline_grounds block saying what was read and which ground, if any, fired; the two lists below are filled from those blocks after the slice walk. Until 2026-08-27 this key held a literal sentence keyed on a coin's name, and both of the grounds it stated had gone stale without anything noticing, because nothing re-read them.
_meta.fee_note: COST REDUCTION, NOT NET ALPHA. The gross volume-weighted mean 10s markout on this flow (~0.52 bps observed at 10s, ~0.56 at 60s) is BELOW the perpetual taker-fee floor (~2.5-4.5 bps) plus funding, so a net trading edge is impossible and is never claimed. Every figure here is a maker COST or a relative reduction in that cost from counterparty-aware screening, never a profit.
_meta.scope_note: Counterfactual on REALIZED markout, not a live fill model: no limit-order-book simulation, no queue/fill-probability, no requote. Declining a wallet = not paying its realized markout cost and forgoing its notional. Single December window, trade-print reference (a cost, not an information edge). This is VALIDATION / ILLUSTRATION of the cost-reduction mechanism, not a powered live-performance claim.

procedure.method: permutation p = (draws at least as extreme + 1) / (usable draws + 1); the observed labelling counts as one draw of its own null, so p is floored at 1/(usable + 1) and is never zero

size_matched_placebo.matched_on: total late notional of the observed toxic set

size_matched_procedure.procedure: notional-matched stratified draw, counted -- NOT a label permutation. Each draw takes wallets across notional strata until its TOTAL LATE NOTIONAL lands nearest the observed toxic set's, so the notional is the axis held and the NUMBER of wallets is not held at all: it is whatever the draw needed and it varies from draw to draw. The p is a Monte Carlo tail over independent draws of THIS procedure. This field read 'label permutation' until 2026-08-30, the name stats.permutation_p writes for every caller, and it was wrong for this null: a label permutation holds the count exactly and shuffles the labels, which is the count-matched placebo beside this one and not this draw. Only the name moved on that date; the counting and every number it produced are unchanged.
size_matched_procedure.method: permutation p = (draws at least as extreme + 1) / (usable draws + 1); the observed labelling counts as one draw of its own null, so p is floored at 1/(usable + 1) and is never zero

size_matched_placebo.size_only_note: UPPER bound on pure size: top decile by NUMBER of wallets ranked on notional concentrates on the largest wallets and turns away more notional than the toxic set; the like-for-like pure-size baseline is the size-matched RANDOM mean.
size_matched_placebo.note: observed toxicity-ranked reduction is the cost cut from declining WHO is toxic; size-matched mean is the cost cut from declining the same HOW-MUCH (notional) at random; the gap is what remains of the cut once the same dollar volume is turned away at random. toxicity_vs_size_matched_p beside it is a MONTE CARLO TAIL PROBABILITY under the draw procedure this block declares -- the share of those draws reaching the observed value -- and NOT a test of the statistical significance of wallet identity. toxicity_beats_size_matched is that tail read against 0.05 and carries no wider claim. Until 2026-08-30 this note called the gap 'significant at toxicity_vs_size_matched_p' and 'the marginal value of toxicity', which asserted more than the draws support; only the wording moved on that date and no number with it.

joint_matched_placebo.seed_entropy: numpy.random.default_rng([seed, chain]) -- one generator per chain, the chain index 0..n_chains-1 as the second entropy element. Passing the recorded scalar alone reproduces chain 0 and only chain 0, because numpy pads the entropy with zeros; chains 1 upward need the two-element list
joint_matched_placebo.matched_on: the NUMBER of wallets in the observed toxic set, held exactly, AND the total late notional of that set, held to within 1.0 per cent -- both axes at once
joint_matched_placebo.stricter_than_size_matched_note: This null constrains MORE than size_matched_placebo beside it, holding both axes where that one holds the volume alone. It does NOT follow that its upper tail is lower, and measured on this run it is not: the joint null's mean reduction sits ABOVE the size-matched null's on four of the five cells that produce both, and level with it on the fifth. Holding the wallet COUNT as well as the volume forces every draw to RESEMBLE the observed toxic set -- the same number of wallets carrying the same dollars -- and a set that resembles it recovers more of its cost reduction, while the neighbour is free to reach the same notional through a handful of giants or a thousand minnows and be UNLIKE the toxic set. So this null stands NEARER the observed value, and clearing it is a stronger result rather than a weaker one. Read the two distributions side by side before reading either number, and note that the two numbers are not of one kind: the neighbour publishes a p-value, this block publishes the share of its own draws that reached the observed value.

region_freedom.note: one_for_one_swaps_in_band counts the wallets of the whole ranked pool within the band of that member, itself included, so one means no other wallet can replace it in a single swap. The paired move is wider and can displace these members, rarely; this count bounds the single-swap move set and not the walk. Read it beside chain_agreement, which is where the consequence shows.

must_fire_on_notional.case: the same NUMBER of wallets, taken as the smallest by late notional

must_fire_on_count.case: the observed toxic set less its smallest-notional member

predicate_calibration.note: the region test is exercised on three sets built from this cell's own ranked wallets every run: one it must accept and one per axis it must refuse. calibrated false is a refusal, not a warning.

chain_agreement.note: every chain's share of draws reaching the observed reduction has to sit within the stated number of binomial standard deviations of the share pooled over the chains; where the pooled share is zero every chain has to be zero. This compares the chains against each other and cannot see a region every chain is equally trapped in.
chain_agreement.location_note: The chains are NOT required to agree about where the null sits, and on this data they do not: the spread above is real and is a property of the region rather than of the budget. Only the tail is tested, because only the tail is what the published tail fraction counts.

refusal_reasons: the 8 independent starts do not agree about the tail: the share of draws reaching the observed reduction of 12.5112 per cent runs [0.02, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.912, 0.0, 0.0, 0.044] across the chains against a pooled 0.122, and the largest departure 0.79 exceeds the allowed 0.062098. The region is not connected under the moves in use on this cell, so a number here would be a property of where one chain happened to start

joint_matched_placebo.claim: over 8 independent starts holding both axes, 0 of 2000 draws reached the observed reduction of 86.7056 per cent, and the largest reduction any draw reached was 76.556 per cent. That count and that maximum are the whole of what this block asserts. This is NOT a statement that the draws are uniform over the region -- uniformity is not established on this data -- and so the fraction beside it is NOT a p-value: it is the share of these draws, with the observed set counted as one of them. What was tested instead is in chain_agreement, and a cell whose independent starts disagree about the tail is refused outright and carries no reduction and no fraction at all -- which cells those are on this run is read from their own refused flag, not asserted here.
joint_matched_placebo.note: the observed toxicity-ranked reduction is compared against sets that decline the SAME NUMBER of wallets and the SAME dollar volume at once, so neither how-many nor how-much is free to explain it. What is left is WHO. Read this tail fraction beside the two single-axis p-values rather than instead of them, and read it as the different kind of number it is: those two are p-values under nulls whose draws are independent and whose distribution is defined, this one is a count of draws from a walk over a region. Each of the three holds a different thing constant, and the three answer three different objections.
